messages:
nina: Heads-up: onboarding sample with generator streaming is leaking goroutines if the caller uses context.WithTimeout. Repro: start a Generator.Stream with ctx from http request, then deadline fires while iter.Next() is blocked handling network/backpressure. The iterator doesn’t unblock immediately and our app goroutine stays stuck.
arthur: Oof. Is the sample using a background context anywhere?
nina: No, we wire req.Context() through, but the iterator's Next() is implemented to block until either new tokens arrive or stream finishes. When deadline triggers, ctx.Done() is closed but Next() sometimes stays blocked waiting on internal read loop because we never wake the user-facing channel.
kelly: This sounds like the iterator doesn't select on ctx.Done() in the public Next path. That will cause caller goroutines to hang. We should either: a) make Next() return false immediately when ctx is cancelled, b) expose NextContext(ctx) to let callers pass a context per iteration, or c) add an explicit Close/Stop method that cancels internal goroutines.
arthur: API wise I'd prefer NextContext(ctx) to avoid breaking callsites. Example:
```go
iter := client.Generator.Stream(reqCtx, req)
for iter.NextContext(ctx) { // user passes the request-scoped ctx or a timeout
    // handle chunk
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil { /* ... */ }
```
That matches patterns in other libs.
nina: Alternatively a Close() that is safe to call from any goroutine would help the sample app which currently does not clean up when http handler deadline fires. Right now the handler returns but iter goroutines still linger until runtime read loop times out.
kelly: We also saw confusing error signals: when ctx deadline fires sometimes iter.Err() returns nil and app assumes clean completion. We should classify errors: ErrCanceledByContext, ErrIteratorClosed, ErrNetworkStall, etc. Typed errors let apps differentiate normal EOF vs cancellation.
arthur: Let's capture minimal repro and file a devex test that asserts: when request ctx cancels, user NextContext returns false promptly and Err() == ErrCanceledByContext. Also assert that no goroutines remain after Close() for the sample app.
nina: Filing ticket with repro and pprof showing leaked goroutines. I can attach the failing sample snippet.
devex-bot: created DEVEX-1308: go-sdk generator iterator: add NextContext + Close + typed cancel errors (link) :spiral_notepad:
kelly: For onboarding docs: show two patterns: 1) short-lived http handler that cancels ctx on timeout and calls iter.Close(), 2) long-running worker pattern that uses NextContext with a derived timeout. Provide example using context.WithTimeout per iteration to avoid head-of-line blocking.
arthur: Also consider adding a small ergonomics helper on the SDK: StreamIteratorFromReq(req) which binds iterator lifetime to req.Context() and auto-closes when context done (uses finalizer/close but explicit preferred). That would simplify sample code but we must be explicit in docs about resource cleanup.
nina: Agree. I'll prepare the repro and a docs PR updating the generator README with patterns and the NextContext example.
devex-bot: linked DEVEX-1308 to CI job devex/ci/iter-cleanup (will run regression) :gear:
